title: All the AI agents that can live in your text messages
summary: AI agents are increasingly integrating directly into text messaging platforms, allowing users to interact with them without downloading separate applications. These agents, such as Caddy and Fambot, can remember context, connect to existing apps like calendars and email, and perform tasks ranging from scheduling appointments and organizing family life to researching trips and online shopping. This development offers a streamlined and convenient way for users to leverage AI for daily tasks, reducing app clutter and simplifying digital interactions.
image_alt: Diagram showing how a user's text message is processed by an AI agent, which then connects to various apps to complete tasks automatically.

title: OpenAI safety employee resigns, claiming the company’s ‘culture is broken’
summary: OpenAI safety employee David Robinson has resigned, asserting that the company's "culture is broken" and inadequate for managing advanced AI risks. Robinson, who led safety report writing for major product launches, argues that OpenAI's "iterative deployment" approach, which relies on trial and error, inherently guarantees periodic failures that are growing in scale. He contends that frontier AI companies must adopt rigorous safety protocols akin to nuclear power plants or airports, with layers of redundancy and careful planning, to prevent catastrophic outcomes as AI systems become more capable.
image_alt: A comparison showing OpenAI's current 'trial and error' approach leading to growing AI risks, contrasted with a proposed 'safety layers' approach for careful planning to prevent failures.

title: Amazon responds to data center backlash, says it no longer uses NDAs
summary: Amazon Web Services has ceased using nondisclosure agreements (NDAs) in its dealings with government agencies for data center approvals. This policy change comes as CEO Matt Garman addresses widespread suspicion and backlash against data centers, which have faced criticism for lack of transparency, water usage, and electricity costs. By eliminating NDAs, Amazon aims to counter over 100 data center moratoriums being considered across the U.S. and prevent what it calls a "losing ticket" for the country's technological future.
image_alt: Diagram showing how Amazon's removal of NDAs aims to shift data center projects from facing delays and public backlash to achieving smoother approvals and progress.
